title: Hospital medication system upgrade
summary: A hospital is deciding how to replace handwritten medication orders with digital prescribing while preserving patient safety and uninterrupted clinical operations.

sections.title: Situation
sections.narrative: The organization wants the benefits of electronic prescribing and barcode verification, but it cannot tolerate a rollout that creates unsafe mixed workflows for controlled drugs or pushes incomplete clinical integration into live use.

entries.text: prevent medication errors while keeping care running
no dual prescribing allowed for controlled drugs
patient safety rules require fully validated workflows before live use
move from paper-only to mixed mode
move from mixed mode to full electronic
direct cutover from paper-only to full electronic

candidate_paths.title: Outcome
candidate_paths.narrative: The operational conclusion is that the hospital has one viable path: complete the dependencies first, then move directly to the validated electronic state.
highlights: mixed-mode prescribing remains inadmissible because it violates safety and regulatory constraints
direct cutover becomes viable only after training, integration, and approval are complete before go-live
